A vehicle imaging apparatus includes a location-determining module configured to identify the position of a remote imaging apparatus relative to the vehicle. The location-determining module receives a tracking signal from a remote transmitter associated with the remote imaging apparatus and uses that signal to determine the remote apparatus’s relative location.

The vehicle imaging apparatus also includes an image receiver that receives image data transmitted by the remote imaging apparatus. An image processor then processes the received image data based on the determined location of the remote imaging apparatus, allowing the images to be interpreted or displayed in the appropriate positional context.

The remote imaging apparatus is configured for mounting on a trailer and includes a camera for capturing images and an image transmitter for sending the captured image data to the vehicle imaging apparatus. Together, the vehicle imaging apparatus, the trailer-mounted remote imaging apparatus, and the associated tracking module form a vehicle imaging system that provides location-aware image capture and processing.
outputs.L4:
A vehicle imaging system is configured to determine the location of a remote camera mounted on a trailer or another structure associated with a vehicle. The remote camera transmits a tracking signal that is received by one or more tracking receivers located on the vehicle. Using characteristics of the received signal—such as signal strength, direction, timing, phase, or a combination of these—the system determines the camera’s position relative to the vehicle. The determined position may include the camera’s distance, direction, orientation, or mounting region on the trailer.

Separately from the tracking signal, the remote camera captures image data and transmits that data to the vehicle through a wired or wireless communication link. A vehicle-mounted controller receives and processes the image data using the previously determined relative location of the camera. For example, the controller may select an appropriate image transformation, correct perspective or distortion, align the remote image with images from vehicle-mounted cameras, or determine where the remote image should appear on an in-vehicle display.

By maintaining separate channels or processing paths for camera tracking and image transmission, the system can identify where the imagery originates without relying solely on the image content. This allows the controller to adapt image processing when the trailer configuration changes, when the camera is moved, or when different trailers or remote cameras are connected to the vehicle. The system may also use the location information to verify that the received image data corresponds to an expected camera position.

The processed imagery can support applications such as trailer monitoring, reversing, parking, lane changes, cargo observation, blind-spot reduction, and transparent-trailer or surround-view displays. Because processing is based on the camera’s actual location relative to the vehicle, the resulting display can be more accurately aligned with the vehicle’s surroundings and presented in a context-sensitive manner. This improves driver awareness and enables more reliable integration of trailer-mounted camera imagery into vehicle assistance and visualization systems.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. It helps identify a specific person, place, object, or idea. We say “the sun,” “the world,” and “the future” because we are referring to something particular or widely understood.

Although it often goes unnoticed, “the” brings clarity and precision to communication. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or confusing. This simple word demonstrates how even the smallest elements of language can have a significant impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a vehicle imaging system that determines the relative location of a trailer-mounted remote camera and processes transmitted image data based on that location.
counterfactuals.output: A vehicle imaging system includes a remote camera configured for mounting on a trailer coupled to a vehicle and for transmitting image data to the vehicle. The system further includes one or more processors configured to determine a location of the remote camera relative to the vehicle and to process the transmitted image data based on the determined location. The relative location may be determined using sensor data, calibration data, vehicle or trailer geometry, wireless signal characteristics, or image data from one or more vehicle-mounted cameras. Processing of the transmitted image data may include selecting, cropping, transforming, stitching, correcting, or overlaying the image data to generate a vehicle-relative view. The processed image data may be presented on a vehicle display to provide a rearward, surround, or trailer-transparent view that accounts for the position and orientation of the remote camera relative to the vehicle.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a formal patent-style disclosure describing a vehicle imaging apparatus, a remote imaging apparatus mounted on a trailer, and a tracking signal used to locate the remote apparatus.
counterfactuals.output:
# VEHICLE AND TRAILER IMAGING SYSTEM WITH REMOTE-APPARATUS TRACKING

## Abstract

A vehicle imaging system includes a vehicle imaging apparatus disposed on a towing vehicle and a remote imaging apparatus removably or permanently mounted on a trailer. The remote imaging apparatus includes an image sensor configured to capture imagery of an environment adjacent to or behind the trailer, a wireless communication circuit configured to transmit image data to the vehicle imaging apparatus, and a tracking-signal source configured to transmit a tracking signal usable to determine a location of the remote imaging apparatus relative to the towing vehicle. The vehicle imaging apparatus includes one or more vehicle-mounted image sensors, a tracking receiver, a processor, and a display interface. The processor determines a position, orientation, or both of the remote imaging apparatus based at least in part on the tracking signal and processes imagery received from the remote imaging apparatus according to the determined position or orientation. The processed imagery may be displayed independently or combined with vehicle-mounted imagery to provide a composite view, including a view in which at least a portion of the trailer appears transparent.

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates generally to imaging systems for vehicles and, more particularly, to systems that use a vehicle-mounted imaging apparatus, a remote imaging apparatus mounted on a trailer, and a tracking signal for locating the remote imaging apparatus relative to the vehicle.

## Background

A trailer coupled to a towing vehicle may obstruct a rearward field of view of a driver and may interfere with vehicle-mounted cameras, mirrors, radar devices, or other environmental sensors. A camera mounted on the trailer can provide imagery of an area behind or alongside the trailer. However, conventional trailer-camera systems may require manual configuration, fixed wiring, or manual identification of the camera's location and orientation.

The spatial relationship between a towing vehicle and a trailer may change during travel as the trailer pivots about a hitch. A remote camera may also be moved between mounting locations, mounted on different trailers, or installed with an unknown orientation. Consequently, received imagery may not accurately align with imagery obtained by the towing vehicle unless the location and orientation of the remote camera are known.

A need therefore exists for an imaging system capable of locating a remote trailer-mounted imaging apparatus and using the determined location to select, transform, combine, or display imagery.

## Summary

In one embodiment, a system includes a vehicle imaging apparatus associated with a towing vehicle and a remote imaging apparatus mounted on a trailer coupled to the towing vehicle. The remote imaging apparatus captures remote image data and communicates the remote image data to the vehicle imaging apparatus. The remote imaging apparatus additionally emits a tracking signal. A tracking receiver associated with the towing vehicle receives the tracking signal, and a processor determines a spatial relationship between the remote imaging apparatus and the towing vehicle.

The spatial relationship may include one or more of a distance, direction, three-dimensional position, mounting height, heading, pitch, roll, yaw, or trailer articulation angle. The processor may use the spatial relationship to identify the remote imaging apparatus, verify that the apparatus is associated with the coupled trailer, select a display mode, compensate for camera movement, transform the remote imagery, or generate a composite image from vehicle and trailer imagery.

The tracking signal may include a radio-frequency signal, an ultra-wideband signal, a Bluetooth signal, a wireless local-area-network signal, an ultrasonic signal, an optical signal, a satellite-positioning message, or any combination thereof. In some embodiments, multiple receivers on the towing vehicle determine the location of the remote imaging apparatus through ranging, angle-of-arrival measurement, time-of-flight measurement, time-difference-of-arrival measurement, received-signal-strength measurement, phase measurement, or triangulation.

## Brief Description of Exemplary Drawings

Although drawings are not included herein, representative drawings may depict:

1. a towing vehicle coupled to a trailer having a remote imaging apparatus;
2. a block diagram of the vehicle imaging apparatus and the remote imaging apparatus;
3. a plurality of tracking receivers positioned at different locations on the towing vehicle;
4. overlapping fields of view of vehicle-mounted and trailer-mounted cameras;
5. a method for locating and pairing the remote imaging apparatus;
6. a method for generating a composite rearward image; and
7. an example display presenting a trailer-transparent view.

## Detailed Description

### System Architecture

A vehicle system includes a towing vehicle, a trailer coupled to the towing vehicle by a hitch assembly, a vehicle imaging apparatus, and a remote imaging apparatus mounted on the trailer.

The vehicle imaging apparatus may include one or more cameras positioned on the towing vehicle. Exemplary locations include a rear fascia, tailgate, roof, side-view mirror, front grille, or passenger compartment. The cameras may capture visible-light, infrared, thermal, depth, or multispectral imagery.

The vehicle imaging apparatus further includes a processor, memory, a wireless communication interface, a tracking receiver, and a display interface. The processor may be a dedicated image processor, an electronic control unit, an infotainment processor, or a distributed combination thereof. The display interface provides image data to an in-vehicle display, instrument cluster, head-up display, mirror-replacement display, mobile device, or remote operator station.

### Remote Imaging Apparatus

The remote imaging apparatus includes a housing supporting at least one remote image sensor. The housing may be permanently attached to the trailer or removably attached using a magnetic mount, mechanical fastener, adhesive mount, rail interface, suction mount, or docking structure.

The remote image sensor may be directed rearward, laterally, downward, or toward a trailer cargo area. Multiple remote image sensors may provide a panoramic, stereoscopic, surround-view, or depth image. The apparatus may additionally include an inertial measurement unit, satellite-positioning receiver, processor, memory, wireless transceiver, tracking-signal source, and power supply.

The power supply may include a rechargeable battery, a trailer electrical connection, a solar cell, or an energy-harvesting device. A charging interface may charge the remote imaging apparatus when the apparatus is docked on the towing vehicle or connected to the trailer electrical system.

The remote image data may be compressed and transmitted wirelessly to the vehicle imaging apparatus. Alternatively, the remote imaging apparatus may communicate through a wired trailer connector, with the tracking signal being transmitted separately or encoded in the wired communication.

### Tracking Signal

The remote imaging apparatus transmits a tracking signal containing or associated with an apparatus identifier. The apparatus identifier may distinguish the remote imaging apparatus from other imaging devices within communication range. The tracking signal may further contain a timestamp, sequence number, authentication value, device status, battery level, positioning information, or orientation information.

In one embodiment, the tracking-signal source is an ultra-wideband transmitter or transceiver. Two or more spatially separated receivers on the towing vehicle measure a range or direction to the remote imaging apparatus. Based on the measurements and known receiver locations, the processor determines a three-dimensional location of the remote imaging apparatus relative to a vehicle coordinate frame.

In another embodiment, the remote imaging apparatus includes a satellite-positioning receiver and transmits geographic coordinates to the vehicle imaging apparatus. The vehicle determines its own coordinates and computes a relative displacement. Differential correction data may be used to improve accuracy.

In further embodiments, the tracking signal comprises a Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, cellular, radio-frequency identification, ultrasonic, infrared, or visible optical signal. Relative location may be estimated from received signal strength, time of flight, phase difference, angle of arrival, visual marker detection, or combinations thereof.

The tracking signal may be transmitted continuously, periodically, in response to vehicle motion, in response to a pairing request, or when image transmission is initiated. A transmission rate may be increased during reversing, turning, hitching, or other operations requiring greater positional accuracy.

### Determination of Relative Position and Orientation

The processor establishes a vehicle coordinate frame having a known relationship to the towing vehicle. The location of each tracking receiver and vehicle-mounted camera may be stored in memory. Measurements derived from the tracking signal are used to determine the position of the remote imaging apparatus in the vehicle coordinate frame.

An orientation of the remote imaging apparatus may be determined from an onboard inertial measurement unit, multiple tracking-signal antennas, image analysis, or comparison with a stored trailer model. The processor may also determine a hitch angle between the towing vehicle and trailer. The hitch angle may be derived from the position of the remote apparatus, a hitch sensor, steering data, wheel-speed data, trailer yaw data, or image-based feature tracking.

Filtering may be applied to reduce noise and reject implausible position changes. For example, a Kalman filter, particle filter, or other state estimator may combine tracking measurements with vehicle speed, steering angle, yaw rate, and trailer geometry.

If the remote apparatus is mounted at an unknown location, the system may perform an automatic calibration procedure. During calibration, the vehicle may move through a predetermined or naturally occurring trajectory while the processor collects tracking and image data. The processor then estimates the remote camera's mounting location, optical axis, field of view, and orientation.

### Pairing and Validation

The vehicle imaging apparatus may discover one or more remote imaging apparatuses within communication range. A candidate apparatus may be selected based on proximity to an expected trailer region, signal identity, stored authorization data, user input, or physical connection through a trailer wiring interface.

Before displaying remote imagery, the processor may verify that the candidate apparatus remains in a spatial region associated with the coupled trailer. This reduces the possibility of displaying imagery from an unrelated trailer or nearby vehicle.

Communication may be authenticated or encrypted. If the tracking signal and image-data transmission use different communication channels, information contained in the tracking signal may be used to authenticate or establish the image-data channel.

### Image Processing and Display

The processor receives remote image data and determines how the image data should be presented based at least in part on the tracked position or orientation of the remote imaging apparatus.

In a first mode, the remote imagery is displayed as a dedicated rear-trailer view. In a second mode, vehicle-mounted imagery and remote imagery are displayed simultaneously. In a third mode, the processor generates a composite image by geometrically transforming and stitching the respective image streams.

For generation of a trailer-transparent view, the processor identifies an image region in which the trailer obstructs a view from a virtual viewpoint. Remote imagery corresponding to the obstructed region is transformed into the virtual viewpoint and inserted into the vehicle imagery. The position and orientation obtained from the tracking signal facilitate alignment of the remote imagery with the vehicle imagery.

The processor may compensate for lens distortion, camera latency, communication latency, vehicle motion, trailer articulation, and differences in exposure or color. Time synchronization may be performed using timestamps included with the image data or tracking signal.

Graphical overlays may identify trailer boundaries, hitch angle, predicted vehicle or trailer paths, distances to objects, blind zones, or the location and orientation of the remote imaging apparatus. If tracking confidence falls below a threshold, the system may suppress image stitching, display the remote image independently, or generate an alert.

### Loss and Recovery Functions

When the remote apparatus ceases transmitting image data or tracking signals, the vehicle imaging apparatus may display the last known location, estimate a current location from a motion model, and notify the operator. If the remote imaging apparatus is detachable, the tracking signal may be used to locate the apparatus after removal from the trailer.

A portable device may receive the tracking signal and display a direction or distance to the remote apparatus. The remote apparatus may emit an audible or visible indication in response to a locate command. Thus, the tracking function may assist both in spatial calibration during vehicle operation and in recovery of a misplaced or detached apparatus.

## Exemplary Method

An exemplary method includes:

1. detecting a remote imaging apparatus within communication range of a towing vehicle;
2. receiving, at one or more vehicle-mounted receivers, a tracking signal transmitted by the remote imaging apparatus;
3. determining a location of the remote imaging apparatus relative to the towing vehicle based on the tracking signal;
4. receiving remote image data captured by the remote imaging apparatus;
5. determining a transformation for the remote image data based at least in part on the determined location;
6. processing the remote image data according to the transformation; and
7. displaying the processed remote image data independently or in combination with image data from a vehicle-mounted image sensor.

The method may further include determining an orientation of the remote imaging apparatus, identifying a trailer articulation angle, authenticating the remote imaging apparatus, and updating the transformation as the trailer moves relative to the towing vehicle.

## Exemplary Claims

1. **A vehicle imaging system comprising:**  
   a vehicle imaging apparatus associated with a towing vehicle, the vehicle imaging apparatus including a processor, a display interface, and at least one tracking receiver; and  
   a remote imaging apparatus configured to be mounted on a trailer coupled to the towing vehicle, the remote imaging apparatus including an image sensor, a communication circuit configured to transmit image data generated by the image sensor, and a tracking-signal source configured to transmit a tracking signal,  
   wherein the processor is configured to determine a location of the remote imaging apparatus relative to the towing vehicle based at least in part on the tracking signal and to process the image data based at least in part on the determined location.

2. **The vehicle imaging system of claim 1**, wherein the tracking signal comprises an ultra-wideband signal, and the vehicle imaging apparatus includes a plurality of spatially separated tracking receivers.

3. **The vehicle imaging system of claim 1**, wherein the processor is configured to determine an orientation of the remote imaging apparatus relative to the towing vehicle.

4. **The vehicle imaging system of claim 3**, wherein the processor is configured to transform the image data according to the location and orientation of the remote imaging apparatus.

5. **The vehicle imaging system of claim 1**, further comprising a vehicle-mounted image sensor, wherein the processor is configured to combine vehicle image data from the vehicle-mounted image sensor with the image data from the remote imaging apparatus.

6. **The vehicle imaging system of claim 5**, wherein the combined image data represents a virtual view through at least a portion of the trailer.

7. **The vehicle imaging system of claim 1**, wherein the tracking signal includes an identifier associated with the remote imaging apparatus, and the processor is configured to authenticate or pair the remote imaging apparatus based on the identifier.

8. **The vehicle imaging system of claim 1**, wherein the processor is configured to determine a trailer articulation angle based at least in part on the location of the remote imaging apparatus.

9. **The vehicle imaging system of claim 1**, wherein the remote imaging apparatus is removably mountable to the trailer and includes a rechargeable power source.

10. **A method of operating a vehicle imaging system, the method comprising:**  
    receiving a tracking signal transmitted by a remote imaging apparatus mounted on a trailer;  
    determining, based at least in part on the tracking signal, a location of the remote imaging apparatus relative to a towing vehicle;  
    receiving image data captured by the remote imaging apparatus;  
    processing the image data according to the determined location; and  
    causing the processed image data to be presented on a display associated with the towing vehicle.

11. **The method of claim 10**, further comprising combining the image data with vehicle image data to generate a composite image from a virtual viewpoint.

12. **The method of claim 10**, further comprising determining that the remote imaging apparatus is positioned within a region associated with the trailer before causing the image data to be presented.

13. **A remote imaging apparatus comprising:**  
    a housing configured for attachment to a trailer;  
    an image sensor supported by the housing;  
    a wireless communication circuit configured to transmit image data captured by the image sensor;  
    a tracking-signal source configured to transmit a tracking signal usable by a towing vehicle to determine a location of the remote imaging apparatus; and  
    a power source configured to supply electrical power to the image sensor, the wireless communication circuit, and the tracking-signal source.

## Conclusion

The described embodiments permit a towing vehicle to locate a trailer-mounted imaging apparatus and to use the resulting spatial information to configure, validate, transform, or combine imagery. Features described in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features of other embodiments, and the disclosed examples are illustrative rather than limiting.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention involving a vehicle receiver that obtains camera images and tracking signals from a remote trailer camera, using numbered component references throughout.
counterfactuals.output:
1. A vehicle monitoring system **(10)** includes a receiver **(12)** installed in or connected to a towing vehicle **(14)** and a remotely located camera unit **(16)** mounted on a trailer **(18)**.

2. The trailer camera unit **(16)** includes a camera **(20)** that captures images of an area around or behind the trailer **(18)**, a tracking module **(22)** that generates tracking signals, and a wireless transmitter **(24)** that sends both the camera images and tracking signals to the receiver **(12)**.

3. The receiver **(12)** includes a wireless interface **(26)** for obtaining the transmitted data and a processor **(28)** for associating the images from the camera **(20)** with the tracking signals from the tracking module **(22)**. The tracking signals may identify the camera unit **(16)** or indicate its position, orientation, motion, or relationship to the towing vehicle **(14)**.

4. A display **(30)** presents the received images to a driver, while the processor **(28)** may use the tracking signals to maintain communication with the correct trailer camera unit **(16)**, select an appropriate image view, compensate for trailer movement, or provide parking and reversing assistance.

5. The invention therefore enables the towing vehicle **(14)** to receive a reliable remote view from the trailer **(18)** without a fixed video cable, while using the tracking module **(22)** and receiver **(12)** to identify, monitor, and manage the camera feed.

counterfactuals.output: A system comprises a vehicle imaging apparatus (2) configured to acquire first image data from an environment of a vehicle, a remote imaging apparatus (3) configured to acquire second image data from a location remote from the vehicle, and a location determining module (10) configured to determine location information associated with the vehicle, the remote imaging apparatus (3), or an imaged object. An image receiver module (7) receives the first and second image data, and an image processor (5) processes the received image data based at least partly on the location information.
